To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the European Union is not a 'normal' international organization and that its history is a history of integration and disintegration.

the European integration project was a success in the sense of the European Commission and the European Parliament, that the EU has become a supranational political system with a strong executive, that the EU was not a 'federal state' in the sense of political science, and that the EU has been successful in the sense of economic and social policy.

the EU is a complex, multi-level system that is not a single entity, that its member states are not equal in terms of their influence, that the EU is not a unitary actor and that the EU has a complex and multi-faceted history.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how and why the EU has become a more contested political project, how the 'ever closer union' has become more fragile, and what the consequences of the EU crisis for the future of European integration are.
the history of the European Union.
the history of European integration, and more broadly with European integration history.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the four reviewed books provide a very valuable contribution to the current debates in European integration history.
the recent crisis of European integration is the beginning of a new phase of integration history, which is characterized by a more complex narrative and the end of the 'ever closer Union'.
the EU and its history are still far too complex to be captured in one book.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these books show that there is a need for a more complex understanding of the European integration process.
the authors of these four books have made a strong case for a more critical, nuanced and less teleological narrative of the EU and European integration history in the last 50 years.
the authors of all four books have in common that they do not see the EU's current crisis as a 'normal' crisis of a political system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the European integration process has not been a linear process of ever closer union. Rather, the EU has experienced phases of crisis and stagnation
we should be more careful in our use of the term 'centrism' when it comes to the study of the EU.
there are many ways to study the EU.
